subject: DPA: security alert, evidence transfer windows & notification SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@protodata.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA — notification timing, evidence sharing, subprocessors

Vivek / team,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. We're reviewing but have a couple of high-priority asks related to incident notification and post-incident cooperation:

- Notification SLA: Protodata requires customer notification within 24 hours of discovery for any incident that affects customer data. Can Redwood commit to that?
- Scope & evidence: We will likely request packet/log exports, retained request IDs, and a timeline of affected resources. What is your standard evidence-transfer window?
- Subprocessors: we need confirmation that you will notify customers if a subprocessor is implicated and that Redwood will coordinate evidence requests involving subprocessors.
- Cross-border transfers: if EU-origin data is affected, what controls do you have to ensure timely transfer of forensic artifacts to our EU team?

Can we get either: (a) a written confirmation of timelines, or (b) a short call this week to align so we can proceed with the DPA redlines? Attached: Protodata_DPA_Questions_v1.docx with annotated sections.

Best,
Claire
Claire Nguyen
Head of Legal & Privacy
Protodata Analytics

---
Attachment: Protodata_DPA_Questions_v1.docx (document with annotated clause references)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@protodata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA — notification timing, evidence sharing, subprocessors

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the chance to align. High level answers below, with a proposed incident-notification annex attached for redline: Redwood_DPA_IncNotify_Annex_v2.pdf.

1) Initial notification SLA: Redwood's standard is to provide "Initial customer notification" within 48 hours of confirming an incident that affects customer data (we define "confirming" as when we have reasonable evidence that an event caused unauthorized access or disclosure). We'll include a short statement in the DPA that we will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify earlier if possible.

2) Preliminary scope & updates: We can provide an initial scope summary within 72 hours of confirmation and subsequent status updates every 72 hours until a root-cause is available.

3) Forensic evidence transfer: Redwood can provide exports (logs, request IDs, relevant traces) under a secure transfer and data handling agreement. Typical delivery cadence: preliminary artifacts within 5 business days, full export within 15 business days, dependent on scope and legal considerations (e.g., third-party logs). We are open to firming this up to 5 business days for high-priority requests; see proposed wording in the annex.

4) Subprocessors: we will notify affected customers when a subprocessor is implicated and will coordinate investigations. We maintain a published subprocessor list (link in footer) and can provide additional contact points/engagement paths for specific subprocessors when necessary.

5) Cross-border transfers: For EU-origin data, we will use the contractual safeguards in the DPA (SCCs or other mechanisms where applicable). Evidence transfer to EU parties will be done over encrypted channels and in accordance with applicable export controls; timing may be impacted by legal holds or local law requests.

Next steps: Rafael / Neha — please review the annex for any legal gaps; Hannah — please check feasibility of 5 business day preliminary artifacts and the secure transfer approach. Claire — happy to schedule a 30-min call if you'd prefer to walk through the annex.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_IncNotify_Annex_v2.pdf (proposed incident notification & evidence transfer wording, draft)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@protodata.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA — notification timing, evidence sharing, subprocessors

Claire / team,

I've reviewed Vivek's annex and the questions. A few legal clarifications / redline requests from our side:

- Notification trigger: we prefer to keep "confirming" as the trigger but will add a customer-facing clause that Redwood will use "commercially reasonable efforts" to provide earlier updates upon credible indicators. We can't commit to a blanket 24-hour confirmed-notification due to the need for initial triage across infrastructure.

- Subprocessor incidents: Redwood will notify customers when a subprocessor is implicated and will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and provide subprocessor artifacts. However, we cannot compel third parties to release raw forensic images; we can coordinate and escalate.

- Evidence transfer timing: Needing to balance forensic integrity and legal review, propose: initial artifacts within 5 business days for high-priority requests (redlined), full export within 15 business days. We'll include a carve-out for data that is under third-party control or subject to law enforcement/third-party subpoenas.

- EU transfers: We'll note that transfers of forensic artifacts will comply with EU data transfer rules; certain exports may require redaction or court orders and could take longer.

I've attached DPA_Redlines_Protodata_v3.pdf with inline edits. Rafael, happy for you to add any commercial/legal risk language.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Legal (Data Protection)
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: DPA_Redlines_Protodata_v3.pdf (legal redlines)

From: Samir Desai <security@protodata.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire@protodata.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA — notification timing, evidence sharing, subprocessors

Thanks for the proposals. Protodata can accept 48 hours initial notification if Redwood will commit to the following clarifications:

- Evidence transfer: we need preliminary artifacts (log slices, request IDs, timeline) within 5 business days. If full forensic images require >5 days, please provide a written schedule for completion and what will be delivered at each milestone.
- Scope definition: please include a short template (fields) describing what Redwood will include in the "initial scope summary" (affected accounts, data types, estimated user count).
- Subprocessor escalation: please confirm a named contact at Redwood who will be responsible for coordinating subprocessor evidence requests (we propose an escalation path into Redwood Security).

We'd like to lock this into the DPA annex and then move to signature. Can we set a call Friday to finalize? Attached: Evidence_Request_Specs.xlsx with fields we'd expect.

—Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Security Operations
Protodata Analytics

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@protodata.com>, Samir Desai <security@protodata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA — notification timing, evidence sharing, subprocessors

Claire / Samir — thanks, and appreciate the pragmatism. Confirming Redwood's stance so you can close your redlines: 

- Initial notification: 48 hours from confirmation (we'll add the phrase "or earlier when feasible" in the annex).
- Initial scope summary: within 72 hours. The annex includes a template with: affected customer IDs, affected product/service, data classes, estimated user scope, and contact for follow-up.
- Evidence transfer: Redwood will provide preliminary artifacts within 5 business days for priority requests. We will follow with a delivery schedule for remaining artifacts (target full export within 15 business days) and will communicate milestone deliveries in each status update.
- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood Security will own subprocessor escalations. Primary contact: Hannah Schmitt (hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com). We will notify the customer when a subprocessor is implicated and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain subprocessor artifacts.

Operational notes:
- Transfers to EU teams will use encrypted SFTP or secure sharelinks with SCP and will comply with SCCs where applicable. Any transfer affected by legal restrictions will be escalated to Neha / Rafael.
- We will not provide unrestricted raw forensic images that would violate third-party or legal restrictions; where applicable we will provide redacted extracts and a documented chain of custody.

Next actions: Vivek will update the annex and circulate by EOD Monday; Neha / Rafael to confirm legal language; Claire to confirm the 5-business-day acceptance and sign the annex if green. Laura — please loop in sales procurement/AM and update the HubSpot deal record once executed.

Thanks all — happy to hop on a Friday call if you still want to talk through the exact wording.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference
